Green Party of England and Wales.crime: Greens focus on crime prevention through youth services and restorative justice, helping offenders take responsibility while giving victims a voice. They advocate for a presumption against custodial sentences under two years. Key policies include ending routine stop and search, making misogyny a hate crime, and establishing a National Commission to move toward a legally regulated, decriminalized drug market.
Green Party of England and Wales.healthcare: The Greens propose a massive investment in the NHS, reaching an additional £28bn annually by 2030. They advocate for pay restoration for junior doctors and a fully public health service by ending all privatization. Policies include guaranteeing rapid GP access, providing an NHS dentist for all, and investing £20bn in hospital building and repairs. They also support free personal care and legalizing assisted dying.
Green Party of England and Wales.housing: The Greens prioritize 150,000 social homes annually and ending Right to Buy. They propose a £29bn retrofit programme for insulation and require all new builds to meet Passivhaus standards. Their "fair deal for renters" includes rent controls, long-term leases, and ending no-fault evictions. Finally, they would grant local authorities first option to purchase empty properties and substandard private rentals.
Green Party of England and Wales.immigration: Greens advocate for an inclusive system by dismantling the Home Office and creating a new Department of Migration. They would abolish the "hostile environment", No Recourse to Public Funds, and the ten-year route to settlement. Pledges include establishing safe routes to sanctuary, ending immigration detention, and removing minimum income requirements for family visas. They also support free NHS access for all visa holders.
Green Party of England and Wales.defence: The Greens propose a fundamental shift toward global peacebuilding and disarmament. They would scrap Trident, sign the UN Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons, and remove all foreign nuclear weapons from UK soil. While supporting NATO’s defensive role, they demand reforms including a ‘No First Use’ nuclear policy. They also pledge to end all arms exports to Israel and military training involving animals.
Green Party of England and Wales.economy: The Greens propose a radical Green Economic Transformation, investing £40 billion annually in decarbonization. This is funded by a carbon tax on polluters and wealth taxes on multi-millionaires. They advocate for bringing water and energy companies back into public ownership. Additional policies include increasing the minimum wage to £15 an hour and moving toward a four-day working week.
Green Party of England and Wales.education: Greens advocate for a fully inclusive system that is publicly funded and free at all stages. They propose abolishing university tuition fees, restoring maintenance grants, and ending high-stakes testing. Key pledges include an £8bn investment in schools, providing a trained counsellor in every school, and bringing academies back under local authority control. They also support a 35-hour weekly childcare offer.
Green Party of England and Wales.environment: The Greens propose a radical Green Economic Transformation, investing £40 billion annually to reach net zero more than a decade before 2050. They would ban all new fossil fuel extraction, introduce a carbon tax, and bring energy and water utilities into public ownership. Their nature plan includes a Rights of Nature Act and protecting 30% of land and sea by 2030.
Green Party of England and Wales.brexit: The Green Party believes full membership of the EU remains the "best option" for the UK and pledges to rejoin as soon as possible. As a first step, they advocate for joining the Customs Union to resolve many of the worst problems resulting from Brexit. They also support a speedy return to the free movement of people and rejoining the Erasmus Programme to restore educational opportunities.
Green Party of England and Wales.entire manifesto: The Greens propose a radical Green Economic Transformation, investing £40bn annually funded by taxing the wealthy and polluters. They advocate for public ownership of energy, water, and railways. Pledges include rejoining the EU, scrapping Trident, and increasing the minimum wage to £15. Their social agenda includes abolishing tuition fees, building 150,000 social homes yearly, and providing free personal care for the elderly and disabled.

Reform UK.crime: Reform UK pledges zero-tolerance policing, aiming to recruit 40,000 new frontline officers. They advocate for automatic life imprisonment for repeat violent offenders and mandatory life for drug trafficking. Proposed reforms include scrapping Diversity, Equality and Inclusion (DE&I) roles in policing, building 10,000 new prison places, and using high-intensity training camps for young offenders to teach discipline and values.
Reform UK.healthcare: Reform UK aims for zero NHS waiting lists through major structural reform. To tackle shortages, they propose a three-year income tax exemption for frontline NHS and social care staff. They offer 20% tax relief on private healthcare and an NHS Voucher Scheme, allowing patients to go private if waiting times for doctors or operations are exceeded. Efficiency measures include cutting managers and opening operating theatres on weekends.
Reform UK.housing: Reform UK focuses on freezing non-essential immigration to reduce housing demand and fast-tracking planning for brownfield sites. They propose a social housing reform that prioritizes local residents who have paid into the system while moving foreign nationals to the back of the queue. They would also scrap Section 24 tax changes for landlords and cut Stamp Duty to 0% for properties below £750,000.
Reform UK.immigration: Reform UK proposes a freeze on all non-essential immigration to protect public services and culture, excepting only essential healthcare skills. They would leave the ECHR and ensure zero illegal immigrants are resettled by returning "small boats" to France. Other measures include deporting foreign criminals, barring student dependants, and introducing a 20% National Insurance rate for employers of foreign workers to incentivise hiring British citizens.
Reform UK.defence: Reform UK plans to increase defense spending to 2.5% of GDP by year three, and 3% within six years. They aim to recruit 30,000 more Army personnel and introduce an urgent pay review to improve retention. Key reforms include an Armed Forces Justice Bill to protect personnel from legal challenges and creating a dedicated Ministerial Department for Veterans to ensure lifetime support.
Reform UK.economy: Reform UK’s "Contract" focuses on slashing government waste and scrapping Net Zero to save £80 billion annually. They aim to "make work pay" by lifting the Income Tax threshold to £20,000, taking 7 million people out of tax. For business, they propose cutting corporation tax to 15% and abolishing business rates for high street SMEs, offset by a new online delivery tax.
Reform UK.education: Reform UK promises a "patriotic curriculum" and a ban on "transgender ideology" in schools. They propose a 20% tax relief on independent education to incentivize private schooling and ease state-school pressure. Other pledges include scrapping interest on student loans, doubling the number of Pupil Referral Units, and requiring universities to offer two-year undergraduate courses to reduce student debt and speed up employment.
Reform UK.environment: Reform UK promises to scrap Net Zero and related subsidies, claiming this will save the public sector £30 billion annually. They prioritize "cheap, secure energy" by fast-tracking North Sea oil and gas licenses and granting shale gas (fracking) licenses. Instead of carbon targets, they focus on environmental protection through increased tree planting, more recycling, and reducing single-use plastics.
Reform UK.brexit: Reform UK calls Brexit the "opportunity of a lifetime" and aims to unlock its benefits by immediate legislative action. They propose scrapping all remaining 6,700 EU laws and abandoning the Windsor Framework, which they argue partitioned the UK down the Irish Sea. They also plan to renegotiate the EU Trade and Cooperation Agreement to remove "level playing field" restrictions that they believe hold Britain back.
Reform UK.entire manifesto: Reform UK's "Contract" focuses on scrapping Net Zero to save £30bn annually and freezing non-essential immigration. They aim to "make work pay" by lifting the Income Tax threshold to £20,000 and cutting corporation tax to 15%. Proposed reforms include zero NHS waiting lists, leaving the ECHR, and introducing a "patriotic curriculum" in schools. They also pledge to scrap HS2 to save £25bn.

Labour Party.crime: Labour’s mission is to "take back our streets" by halving serious violent crime and restoring police confidence. They promise 13,000 additional neighborhood officers and PCSOs. Key policies include banning zombie knives, introducing "Respect Orders" for persistent antisocial behavior, and creating specialist rape units in every force. They also propose a "Hillsborough Law" and a new Border Security Command to "smash" criminal boat gangs.
Labour Party.healthcare: Labour’s mission is to build an NHS fit for the future, ensuring it remains publicly owned and funded. They pledge to cut waiting times by delivering 40,000 more weekly appointments and doubling cancer scanners. Key priorities include a Dentistry Rescue Plan, recruiting 8,500 mental health staff, and restoring the family doctor. Additionally, they plan to establish a National Care Service with consistent standards.
Labour Party.housing: Labour intends to build 1.5 million homes by restoring mandatory targets and fast-tracking urban brownfield development. They propose a new generation of New Towns and the release of "grey belt" land. Key reforms include immediately abolishing no-fault evictions, ending the leasehold system, and introducing a permanent mortgage guarantee scheme for first-time buyers to support those with smaller deposits.
Labour Party.immigration: Labour pledges to reduce net migration by linking immigration to skills policy and ending long-term reliance on overseas workers through workforce training plans. They will scrap the Rwanda scheme, instead creating a Border Security Command with specialist investigators to "smash" smuggling gangs. The asylum system will be restored through clearing backlogs, ending hotel use, and creating a new returns and enforcement unit.
Labour Party.defence: Labour’s commitment to the UK’s nuclear deterrent and NATO is "unshakeable". They will conduct a Strategic Defence Review in their first year to assess threats and set a path to spending 2.5% of GDP on defense. Key policies include putting the Armed Forces Covenant fully into law, establishing an independent Armed Forces Commissioner, and creating a new defense industrial strategy to support UK supply chains.
Labour Party.economy: Labour’s first mission is to kickstart economic growth to achieve the highest sustained growth in the G7. They promise economic stability through strict fiscal rules and a new partnership with business via a statutory Industrial Strategy Council. A £7.3 billion National Wealth Fund will support jobs in clean energy and infrastructure. They pledge not to raise National Insurance, Income Tax, or VAT for working people.
Labour Party.education: Labour aims to "break the glass ceiling" by recruiting 6,500 new expert teachers and providing specialist mental health support in every school. They propose funding free breakfast clubs in every primary school and opening 3,000 new nurseries by repurposing school space. To pay for these measures, they will end the VAT exemption and business rates relief for private schools.
Labour Party.environment: Labour’s mission is to make Britain a clean energy superpower, targeting a zero-carbon electricity system by 2030. They will establish Great British Energy, a publicly owned company, and a National Wealth Fund to invest in green industries. Key policies include banning new oil and gas licenses, doubling onshore wind, and quadrupling offshore wind, alongside a massive home insulation upgrade plan.
Labour Party.brexit: Labour intends to "make Brexit work" while remaining outside of the EU, ruling out any return to the Single Market, Customs Union, or freedom of movement. They plan to reset the relationship by tearing down unnecessary trade barriers and negotiating a veterinary agreement to reduce border checks. Additionally, they seek a new UK-EU security pact and mutual recognition of professional qualifications.
Labour Party.entire manifesto: Labour's "Plan for Change" is built on five national missions: growth, clean energy, safer streets, opportunity, and an NHS fit for the future. They prioritize economic stability through strict fiscal rules and a new Industrial Strategy Council. Key initiatives include Great British Energy, a National Wealth Fund for jobs, and recruiting 6,500 new teachers. They also pledge to "smash" criminal gangs with a new Border Security Command.

Conservative and Unionist Party.crime: The Conservatives plan to recruit 8,000 more full-time police officers to ensure a dedicated presence in every neighborhood. They focus on tougher sentencing, including life without parole for the most heinous murders and requiring serious sexual offenders to serve their entire sentence. Other measures include hotspot policing for anti-social behavior, facial recognition technology, and building 20,000 new prison places.
Conservative and Unionist Party.healthcare: The Conservatives plan to increase NHS spending above inflation annually. They aim to recruit 92,000 more nurses and 28,000 more doctors, fulfilling the Long-Term Workforce Plan. Healthcare will move closer to patients through modernised GP surgeries, 50 new Community Diagnostic Centres, and an expanded Pharmacy First scheme. They also pledge to deliver 40 new hospitals by 2030 and implement a Dental Recovery Plan for more appointments.
Conservative and Unionist Party.housing: The Conservatives pledge to build 1.6 million homes in England, focusing on brownfield land and urban regeneration while protecting the Green Belt. They plan to permanently abolish Stamp Duty for first-time buyers up to £425,000 and introduce a new Help to Buy scheme. Other measures include ending Section 21 no-fault evictions and introducing UK connection tests for social housing eligibility.
Conservative and Unionist Party.immigration: The Conservatives focus on reducing numbers through a binding legal cap on work and family visas that will fall every year. They aim to "stop the boats" by permanently removing illegal migrants to Rwanda, prioritising national security over foreign court jurisdictions. Other measures include increasing the skilled worker salary threshold to £38,700 and banning care workers from bringing dependants.
Conservative and Unionist Party.defence: The Conservatives pledge to increase defense spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030, ensuring the UK remains the largest defense power in Europe. They introduce mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds, including a year-long military placement for some. Pledges include modernizing the Trident nuclear deterrent, investing £10 billion in munitions production, and creating new partnerships like AUKUS to meet global threats.
Conservative and Unionist Party.economy: The Conservatives emphasize economic stability by sticking to a plan focused on cutting taxes and reducing debt. Their primary pledges include halving employee National Insurance to 6% and eventually abolishing it for the self-employed. They intend to maintain the Triple Lock Plus for pensioners and support families through expanded free childcare. Business support focuses on permanent full expensing for capital investment and keeping corporation tax at 25%.
Conservative and Unionist Party.education: The Conservatives focus on driving up standards by protecting day-to-day school spending per pupil and recruiting more teachers through bonuses. Key pledges include introducing mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds and creating 100,000 high-quality apprenticeships by curbing "poor-quality" degrees. They plan to ban mobile phones in schools and replace A-levels and T-levels with the Advanced British Standard.
Conservative and Unionist Party.environment: The Conservatives commit to a pragmatic and affordable transition to net zero by 2050, ruling out new green levies and frequent flyer taxes. They prioritize energy security through annual North Sea oil and gas licensing and a significant expansion of nuclear power. Their plan includes trebling offshore wind capacity and investing £6 billion in energy efficiency to make a million homes warmer.
Conservative and Unionist Party.brexit: The Conservatives pledge to seize "Brexit freedoms" by signing further trade deals, such as joining the CPTPP, and cutting red tape for businesses. They plan to repeal or reform over half of the inherited EU laws by 2026. While building on the Trade and Cooperation Agreement, they will reject any dynamic alignment or submission to the CJEU that would infringe on UK legal sovereignty.
Conservative and Unionist Party.entire manifesto: The Conservatives focus on economic stability through tax cuts, including the Triple Lock Plus for pensioners and lower National Insurance. They propose mandatory National Service for 18-year-olds and a legal cap on immigration to ensure numbers fall. Healthcare plans involve recruiting thousands more staff, while housing policy aims to deliver 1.6 million homes. They also pledge to increase defence spending to 2.5% of GDP by 2030.

Scottish National Party (SNP).crime: The SNP advocates for a public health approach to the drug crisis, including decriminalizing personal use and introducing supervised consumption facilities. They prioritize rejoining the EU to restore access to international crime-fighting ecosystems. Key pledges include introducing Martyn’s Law, enforcing the Online Safety Act, and demanding the refund of £175m in VAT owed to Scotland’s emergency services to invest in local safety.
Scottish National Party (SNP).healthcare: The SNP plans to protect Scotland’s NHS from "Westminster privatisation and austerity" through a Bill to keep the service in public hands. They demand that the UK Government increase NHS England funding by £16bn annually, providing an extra £1.6bn for NHS Scotland. Priorities include investing £300m locally to reduce waiting times, supporting overseas care workers’ right to bring families, and addressing Brexit-related medicine shortages.
Scottish National Party (SNP).housing: The SNP aims to tackle the housing emergency caused by underinvestment by restoring capital budget cuts and devolving Housing Benefit and Local Housing Allowance. They advocate for an annual uplift of LHA to reflect actual rental costs and want to scrap the "bedroom tax". To support buyers, they propose reintroducing a Help to Buy ISA and improving accommodation standards for asylum seekers.
Scottish National Party (SNP).immigration: The SNP demands the devolution of immigration powers to create a bespoke migration system for Scotland that meets local demographic and economic needs. They would scrap the Rwanda scheme and the "hostile environment," advocating for the right to work for asylum seekers. Key proposals include a rural visa pilot scheme, expanding shortage occupation lists, and re-entering the EU to restore freedom of movement.
Scottish National Party (SNP).defence: The SNP demands the scrapping of Trident, arguing the billions saved should be reinvested in conventional defense and public services. They advocate for a statutory Armed Forces Representative Body and want to raise the minimum recruitment age to 18. Their security focus includes countering disinformation and protecting critical infrastructure, while supporting continued military aid to Ukraine against Russian aggression.
Scottish National Party (SNP).economy: The SNP argues that independence is essential to escape "Westminster austerity" and rejoin the EU single market. They demand the devolution of all tax powers, including National Insurance and VAT, to create a more progressive system. They propose new fiscal rules to allow for greater borrowing for investment and call for a £28 billion annual investment in the green economy.
Scottish National Party (SNP).education: The SNP emphasizes defending free university tuition in Scotland and rejoining the EU to restore the Erasmus+ scheme. They demand the reversal of UK capital budget cuts to fund new schools and hospitals. The party supports the devolution of all tax powers to create a more progressive system and has already expanded free childcare to save families an average of £5,500 annually.
Scottish National Party (SNP).environment: The SNP targets net zero by 2045 for Scotland and demands the devolution of energy regulation and pricing. They call for a £28 billion annual UK investment in the green economy and a matched £500 million Just Transition Fund for North East workers. The party opposes new nuclear power, seeks to ban new coal licenses, and demands fair funding for Scotland’s peatland and forestry.
Scottish National Party (SNP).brexit: The SNP describes Brexit as a "disaster" for Scotland and pledges to rejoin the EU to reverse its economic damage. They aim to re-enter the Single Market, restoring freedom of movement and access to programs like Erasmus+. They argue independence is the only way for Scotland to regain what was lost and bypass the "Westminster conspiracy of silence" regarding Brexit harms.
Scottish National Party (SNP).entire manifesto: The SNP offers a left-of-centre vision focused on achieving independence to escape Westminster's "broken system". They pledge to rejoin the EU to reverse Brexit harms and restore freedom of movement. Key priorities include protecting the NHS from privatization, ending austerity through increased investment, and scrapping the Trident nuclear program. They also advocate for a public health approach to the drug death crisis.

Plaid Cymru.crime: Plaid Cymru demands the full transfer of policing and justice powers to Wales to create a "Welsh way" of justice. They propose creating a Welsh Minister for Justice and a Victims Commissioner for Wales. Key policies include a Domestic Abuse Register, community-based women's centers, and soft drug decriminalization to focus resources on organized trade. They also advocate for bringing private prisons back under public control.
Plaid Cymru.healthcare: Plaid Cymru advocates for a needs-based funding model to recruit 500 GPs and ensure wage restoration for staff. They propose a Stop Cancer Strategy to catch and treat cancers earlier and intend to create a National Care Service for Wales, making social care free at the point of use. Other measures include opening a new dental school in Bangor and reviewing NHS governance to strengthen accountability.
Plaid Cymru.housing: Plaid Cymru advocates for a Right to Adequate Housing and a significant expansion of social and municipal housing. They support local authorities building council homes and want to tackle homelessness through the Housing First model. To protect communities, they propose caps and registration for second homes, alongside a new Bill to introduce rent controls and other market interventions to ensure local affordability.
Plaid Cymru.immigration: Plaid Cymru demands the devolution of migration powers to Wales, including the ability to set a Wales-specific Shortage Occupation List. They strongly oppose the Rwanda scheme and "hostile environment," seeking to repeal the Illegal Migration Act. Pledges include restoring free transport for refugees, removing visa restrictions on care worker dependants, and establishing safe routes for asylum seekers through processing in third countries or embassies.
Plaid Cymru.defence: Plaid Cymru opposes nuclear weapons and renewal of Trident, preferring investment in conventional defense and peaceful conflict resolution. They believe the Senedd should be consulted before any UK military intervention. Other priorities include a review of arms export controls, withdrawing from the international arms trade, and ensuring War Pensions are not counted as income for veterans' benefit assessments.
Plaid Cymru.economy: Plaid Cymru advocates for fair funding for Wales through a new needs-based settlement. They demand full control over economic levers, including the power to set Wales-specific income tax bands. Their "Welsh Green New Deal" focuses on creating highly skilled jobs in emerging sectors. They also support increasing windfall taxes and devolving the Crown Estate to Wales to build local prosperity.
Plaid Cymru.education: Plaid Cymru demands fair funding for Wales to recruit 5,000 teachers and support staff. They aim to provide free school meals for all primary and secondary pupils and establish Meithrin Cymru, a free Welsh-medium early years service. The manifesto proposes making university education free again, introducing a Lifetime Learning Allowance, and passing a Welsh Language Education Act to achieve universal Welsh-medium education.
Plaid Cymru.environment: Plaid Cymru reaffirms its commitment to reaching net zero in Wales by 2035 and reversing biodiversity decline by 2030. They demand full control over Wales’s natural resources, including devolving the Crown Estate to create green jobs. They oppose new nuclear power and new oil and gas licenses, instead advocating for a Welsh Green New Deal and a national energy company, Ynni Cymru.
Plaid Cymru.brexit: Plaid Cymru advocates for re-joining the EU in the long term, recognizing Brexit as a failure for Wales. In the interim, they believe the UK should join the European Single Market and Customs Union immediately to mitigate economic damage and reduce administrative costs. They also support rejoining pan-European programs like Erasmus+ and restoring freedom of movement to benefit Welsh university and creative sectors.
Plaid Cymru.entire manifesto: Plaid Cymru demands fair funding for Wales to end "economic unfairness". They advocate for rejoining the EU Single Market and gaining full control over Welsh natural resources, including the Crown Estate. Key proposals include recruiting 500 GPs, creating a National Care Service for Wales, and implementing a Welsh Green New Deal to create jobs in emerging sectors. They also prioritize tackling child poverty as a major goal.

Liberal Democrat Party.crime: The Liberal Democrats aim to restore community policing and guarantee that every burglary is properly investigated. They propose replacing Police and Crime Commissioners with local Police Boards. Key pledges include ending the disproportionate use of Stop and Search, introducing a duty of candour for public officials, and legalizing a regulated cannabis market to free up police resources. They also prioritize rehabilitation to reduce reoffending.
Liberal Democrat Party.healthcare: The Liberal Democrats promise a new right to see a GP within seven days, supported by 8,000 more doctors. They prioritize fixing social care by introducing free personal care and establishing a higher Carer’s Minimum Wage. Key pledges include a guarantee for urgent cancer treatment within 62 days, access to an NHS dentist for everyone, and placing a dedicated mental health professional in every primary and secondary school.
Liberal Democrat Party.housing: The Liberal Democrats aim to build 380,000 homes annually, including 150,000 for social rent, partly through ten new garden cities. They plan to abolish residential leaseholds, ban no-fault evictions, and introduce a "Rent to Own" model for social housing. Additionally, they would empower local authorities to end Right to Buy and increase council tax by up to 500% on second homes.
Liberal Democrat Party.immigration: The Liberal Democrats seek to end the "Hostile Environment" and scrap the Rwanda scheme and Illegal Migration Act. They propose transferring work visa policy to economic departments and replacing arbitrary salary thresholds with a merit-based system. Key pledges include safe and legal routes for refugees, granting asylum seekers the right to work after three months, and rejoining the EU's Erasmus Plus and youth mobility schemes.
Liberal Democrat Party.defence: The Liberal Democrats aim to reverse the Conservative cuts to the Army, increasing regular troop numbers to over 100,000. They support an ambition to spend 2.5% of GDP on defense and maintain the nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament. They advocate for closer defense cooperation with the EU, a parliamentary vote before military action, and stricter controls on arms exports to human rights abusers.
Liberal Democrat Party.economy: The Liberal Democrats prioritize investing in green infrastructure and renewable power to drive recovery. They aim to fix the UK’s relationship with Europe to tear down trade barriers. Their tax policy includes reversing Conservative tax cuts for big banks, increasing the Digital Services Tax, and a windfall tax on oil and gas profits. They also propose replacing business rates with a Commercial Landowner Levy.
Liberal Democrat Party.education: The Liberal Democrats prioritize the "best investment" in children by putting a mental health professional in every school and extending free school meals to all children in poverty. They advocate for increasing per-pupil funding above inflation and repairing crumbling buildings. Higher education proposals include reinstating maintenance grants for disadvantaged students and creating £5,000 Lifelong Skills Grants for all adults.
Liberal Democrat Party.environment: The Liberal Democrats pledge to reach net zero by 2045 and generate 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030. They advocate for a "rooftop solar revolution" and an emergency home energy upgrade program. To protect nature, they would double nature by 2050, pass a Clean Air Act, and transform water companies into public benefit entities to end the scandal of sewage dumping.
Liberal Democrat Party.brexit: The Liberal Democrats outline a four-stage roadmap to eventually rejoin the EU. Immediate steps include fixing the "broken relationship" with Europe, participating in EU agencies like Erasmus+, and negotiating veterinary and plant health agreements. Their long-term goal is to join the Single Market and restore trust, arguing that re-entry will rebuild the economy and provide prosperity for citizens.
Liberal Democrat Party.entire manifesto: The Liberal Democrats offer a "Fair Deal" centered on re-establishing a relationship with the EU and moving toward eventually rejoining. They prioritize investing in renewables and home insulation to drive growth. Healthcare pledges include a new right to see a GP within seven days and fixing social care with free personal care. They also advocate for proportional representation and a written federal constitution for the UK.

Alliance Party.crime: Alliance emphasizes human rights and the rule of law as the "cornerstones of safety". They advocate for deeper EU policing cooperation via Europol. A priority is replacing the Legacy Act with a victim-supported alternative. They also support scrapping "authoritarian" anti-protest laws, better regulation of AI and social media for child safety, and a trans-inclusive ban on conversion therapy.
Alliance Party.healthcare: Alliance calls for an improved financial settlement reflecting Northern Ireland's healthcare needs. They focus on better health outcomes through early intervention and inclusive education. Fiscal reforms would involve revising rules to unlock funding for public services. Their immigration policy seeks to scrap the ban on dependents for those on Health and Care Worker visas to address staff shortages and support international healthcare professionals.
Alliance Party.housing: Alliance proposes a UK-wide emergency retrofitting programme to enhance energy efficiency in social and private rented housing. They seek to end the "bedroom tax" and benefit caps. Their immigration policy includes moving away from privatized asylum accommodation toward a not-for-profit system integrated into communities, while placing a statutory duty on providers to prevent homelessness for those leaving supported asylum housing.
Alliance Party.immigration: Alliance supports a compassionate, welcoming immigration system and opposes the "hostile environment". They would repeal the Illegal Migration Act, scrap the Rwanda scheme, and establish safe routes for asylum seekers. Pledges include overhauling the visa system to make it affordable, removing minimum salary thresholds for family visas, and granting asylum seekers the right to work after three months.
Alliance Party.defence: Alliance views NATO as the cornerstone of UK defense and supports a full review to increase spending. They advocate for a formal defense agreement with the EU and deeper intelligence cooperation. Pledges include ensuring NI companies get a fair share of MoD procurement, limiting military intervention to a last resort with an exit strategy, and leading multilateral efforts to reduce nuclear stockpiles.
Alliance Party.economy: Alliance calls for an improved financial settlement for Northern Ireland and a "Green New Deal" to create thousands of jobs. They aim to exploit NI’s dual market access under the Windsor Framework to boost growth. Their fiscal policy includes progressive taxation on the super-wealthy and implementing carbon taxes. They also demand that the Apprenticeship Levy raised in Northern Ireland be ringfenced for local skills reinvestment.
Alliance Party.education: Alliance advocates for a shared future through integrated education and a successor to the Fresh Start capital fund. They propose a new Affordable Childcare Scheme for Northern Ireland and rejoining Erasmus Plus. Key policies include reviewing student finance, ringfencing the Apprenticeship Levy for local skills, and granting international students two-year post-graduation work visas to meet the needs of the regional economy.
Alliance Party.environment: Alliance advocates for a Green New Deal to decarbonize the economy while creating thousands of jobs. They propose revising fiscal rules to account for the costs of environmental inaction and implementing carbon taxes. Key pledges include ending fossil fuel use, banning fracking and new coal mines, and reversing new oil and gas licenses, alongside a UK-wide emergency retrofitting program for homes.
Alliance Party.brexit: Alliance views Brexit as "fundamentally destructive" and advocates for rejoining the EU at the earliest opportunity. In the interim, they seek to join the Single Market and Customs Union to soften its impact. They support improving the implementation of the Windsor Framework to preserve dual market access, while campaigning for a comprehensive UK-EU veterinary agreement and a return to freedom of movement.
Alliance Party.entire manifesto: Alliance seeks to reform Stormont to prevent any single party from blocking progress. They advocate for a Green New Deal to decarbonize the economy and a return to the EU at the earliest opportunity. Key goals include securing an improved financial settlement for NI, expanding inclusive education, and delivering affordable childcare. They champion human rights, proposing to replace the Legacy Act and scrap "authoritarian" anti-protest laws.

Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.crime: The SDLP’s overriding priority is repealing the Legacy Act to stand with victims for truth and justice. They advocate for a representative PSNI, focusing on recruiting more officers from the Catholic tradition. Key policies include ending paramilitarism, implementing an Ending Violence Against Women and Girls Strategy, and introducing standalone hate crime legislation. They also support prison reforms focused on rehabilitation.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.healthcare: The SDLP calls for a "Marshall Plan" style intervention to transform Northern Ireland’s health service. They advocate for fair pay and safe staffing levels, making representations directly to the Treasury. Pledges include dedicated resources to reduce waiting lists, expanding multi-disciplinary teams, and establishing a government-backed indemnity scheme for GPs to prevent closures. They also support provision of gender-affirming healthcare and equal access for refugees.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.housing: The SDLP fights for adequate funding for the Northern Ireland Executive to address the housing crisis and build more social homes. They propose reforming the planning system to prioritize large-scale developments and align growth with social and environmental objectives. Additionally, they advocate for equal opportunities for refugees and asylum seekers to access housing as part of a broader commitment to community integration.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.immigration: The SDLP seeks to repeal the Rwanda scheme and other restrictive asylum legislation, advocating for safe and legal routes for refugees. They support ending the ban on asylum seekers working and ensuring equal access to health, education, and housing. A major priority is establishing a Palestinian Visa Scheme to help displaced people. They also stand against hate crimes and promote the full inclusion of new communities.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.defence: The SDLP’s defense focus centers on the rule of law and human rights. They strongly advocate for repealing the Legacy Act to restore justice for victims of the Troubles. They support a 0.7% international aid target and emphasize the need for a "Marshall Plan" for public services rather than military expansion. They remain committed to international law and compliance with the Windsor Framework.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.economy: The SDLP advocates for a prosperous and regionally balanced economy that maximizes the advantages of dual-market access. They seek the devolution of additional fiscal powers, including Air Passenger Duty and tourism VAT. To tackle poverty, they propose an "Essentials Guarantee" within Universal Credit and a windfall tax on energy giants to fund a Green Prosperity Plan.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.education: The SDLP demands urgent investment to ensure every child has a "fair start". They support above-inflation pay rises for teachers, an overhaul of SEN provision, and a cap on school uniform costs. A major priority is expanding Magee University to 10,000 students. They also seek a 35% tax-free childcare rate and the devolution of the Apprenticeship Levy.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.environment: The SDLP supports ambitious climate legislation, including the Climate and Nature Bill, to mandate targets and a just transition. They campaign for an independent Environmental Protection Agency for Northern Ireland and a dedicated recovery plan for Lough Neagh. Other policies include a green jobs levy on large corporations, a Just Transition Fund for Agriculture, and a new Clean Air Act.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.brexit: The SDLP considers Brexit a disaster that severed Northern Ireland’s vital links to European markets. They believe re-joining the EU is only possible through Irish reunification in an agreed Ireland. They aim to seize the unique trading advantages of dual-market access under the Windsor Framework while working to restore Northern Ireland’s voice in Europe, including the restoration of MEPs.
Social Democratic and Labour Party (SDLP.entire manifesto: The SDLP emphasizes removing the Tory government to end 14 years of "disastrous" austerity. They advocate for Irish reunification as the path back to the EU and dual-market trading advantages. Priorities include a Green Prosperity Plan, additional health investment to cut waiting lists, and repealing the Legacy Act. They also support recognizing the State of Palestine and protecting workers' rights.

Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).crime: The UUP supports a "police first" approach, aiming for a headcount of 7,500 officers. They seek to speed up justice and press for stronger sentences for violent re-offenders, including a review of "50/50" custodial sentences. Key goals include putting paramilitary gangs out of business through asset seizure and repealing the Legacy Act, which they argue denies justice for victims while giving amnesty to perpetrators.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).healthcare: The UUP views the health and wellbeing of Northern Ireland's people as its number one priority. They aim to build a world-leading system by focusing on improved productivity and efficiency. Key commitments include a reconfiguration blueprint, maintaining pay parity, and reducing reliance on expensive agency workers. They also plan to empower primary care to deliver elective services and support the UK Menopause Taskforce.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).housing: The UUP acknowledges a pressing crisis of surging prices and homelessness, advocating for a comprehensive housing strategy developed in collaboration between the UK Government and devolved administrations. They emphasize security of tenure for citizens and believe housing policy must be integrated with other life aspects, such as health and education, to effectively improve quality of life and address the multi-faceted nature of the crisis.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).immigration: The UUP supports an open, transparent, and fair immigration system that targets traffickers while welcoming those who contribute to society. They advocate for a zero-tolerance policy on illegal immigration but want genuine asylum seekers, especially families and healthcare professionals, to have applications fast-tracked. Key pledges include tripling the number of asylum staff and supporting a Racial Equality Strategy to ensure newcomers feel safe and isolation is addressed.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).defence: The UUP supports increasing UK defense spending to 2.5% of GDP and maintaining the independent nuclear deterrent. They propose establishing a Naval Base in Northern Ireland and reverting Aldergrove to a full RAF station to protect western approaches. They also pledge to maintain a minimum of 3,000 personnel in NI and advocate for an LGBT+ veteran financial redress scheme.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).economy: The UUP’s "Prosperity Agenda" focuses on growing the economy through Foreign Direct Investment and supporting SMEs. They propose designating all Northern Ireland ports and airports as Freeports to maximize trade benefits. Key pledges include gradually reducing corporation tax to 15% and matching the Republic of Ireland’s lower VAT rate for leisure and hospitality to ensure local businesses remain competitive.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).education: The UUP envisions a single, integrated education system that integrates children of all abilities. They advocate for fair pay for the "entire multidisciplinary team" and secure funding for therapeutic learning environments. The party proposes a Northern Ireland Job Skills Fund, investing at least £35m annually, and emphasizes the importance of affordable early education and childcare for holistic child development.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).environment: The UUP is dedicated to Northern Ireland making a "fair contribution" to UK net zero targets, striving for at least an 82% reduction in greenhouse gases by 2050. They support the UK’s Ten Point Plan for a Green Industrial Revolution and aim to plant more trees to help nature recover. A major local priority is preserving the ecological integrity of Lough Neagh.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).brexit: The UUP acknowledges the Windsor Framework as a "stepping-stone" in addressing challenges from the NI Protocol, which they campaigned against. They remain dedicated to safeguarding Northern Ireland’s position within the Union and restoring its full place within the UK internal market. They pledge to scrutinize future negotiations between Westminster and the EU to challenge any aspects of the Framework that might undermine sovereignty.
Ulster Unionist Party (UUP).entire manifesto: The UUP’s "Prosperity Agenda" focuses on growing the economy through Foreign Direct Investment and supporting SMEs. They are dedicated to strengthening the Union while robustly challenging the Windsor Framework. Key priorities include protecting the healthcare system, building an integrated education system, and implementing a comprehensive housing strategy. Their delivery is underpinned by the "5Ps": people, place, prosperity, public services, and peace.

Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).crime: TUV demands an end to "two-tier policing" and 50/50 recruitment, insisting on merit-based hiring. They argue policing has been compromised by the "peace process" and demand investigations into historic IRA criminality. Key goals include changing the definition of a victim to exclude perpetrators, rejecting "truth commissions," and opposing the Legacy Act. They share Reform UK’s platform of zero-tolerance policing and higher standards.
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).healthcare: TUV prioritizes long-term investment in frontline staff, advocating for "doctors and nurses, not directors". They oppose the closure of minor injury units and support increased funding for community mental health and early intervention. To address staff shortages, they propose a Nursing Reserve Service of retired professionals. Unashamedly pro-life, the TUV opposes the commissioning of abortion services, focusing the NHS strictly on saving lives.
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).housing: The TUV advocates for urban renewal through a "one house down, one house up" policy and prioritizes proactive maintenance for social tenants, including addressing mould. They demand a reform of the housing points system to give homeless individuals more time to find accommodation. Sharing Reform UK's platform, they also support cutting Stamp Duty to 0% below £750,000 to boost housebuilding and economic activity.
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).immigration: The TUV shares Reform UK’s immigration platform, advocating for a freeze on non-essential immigration and leaving the ECHR to "stop the boats". They argue Northern Ireland must not become a "magnet" for illegal migrants due to the Sea Border and demand a robust UK-wide migration policy. Pledges include secure offshore detention for illegal arrivals, immediate deportation of foreign criminals, and a new Employer Immigration Tax.
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).defence: The TUV shares Reform UK’s defense platform, criticizing politicians for sending under-equipped troops abroad while cutting the Army to its smallest size in centuries. They demand a reform of the Military Covenant to ensure veterans in Northern Ireland receive equitable support. They argue that removing the Irish Sea Border is essential to allow the whole UK to benefit from post-Brexit global security opportunities.
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).economy: TUV shares a common economic platform with Reform UK, advocating for a taxation system that "rewards effort". Their primary economic focus is the removal of the Irish Sea border, which they argue disrupts supply chains and increases costs. They support lifting Income Tax thresholds, cutting energy taxes, and slashing red tape. They also demand a fair funding deal for Northern Ireland's essential services.
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).education: The TUV identifies tackling educational underachievement, particularly for the Protestant working class, as its top priority. They remain committed to academic selection and grammar schools while proposing an overhaul of the curriculum and teacher pay. The manifesto unashamedly opposes the "progressive agenda" and gender identity teaching in schools, while demanding that all childcare Barnett consequentials be spent directly on childcare provision.
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).environment: The TUV shares Reform UK’s environmental platform, advocating for the removal of "hidden green levies" and the scrapping of Net Zero targets. They argue that current climate policies increase household bills and disrupt the economy. Their focus is on cutting energy taxes, including VAT on energy bills and fuel duty, while rejecting environmental levies they believe are "crippling our economy".
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).brexit: The TUV demands a "completion of a full Brexit" for Northern Ireland, rejecting the "Sea Border" and the "sovereignty-grabbing Protocol". They advocate for abandoning the Windsor Framework and restoring Northern Ireland as a full, equal part of the UK with no application of EU law. They propose "Mutual Enforcement" as a democratic solution to manage the border without disenfranchising citizens.
Traditional Unionist Voice (TUV).entire manifesto: The TUV's primary mission is to restore the Union by rejecting the Irish Sea border and completing a "full Brexit". They share Reform UK's economic platform, supporting lower taxes and merit-based policing. Pledges include freezing non-essential immigration, leaving the ECHR, and opposing the Legacy Act. They are unashamedly pro-life, opposing abortion services, and want to maintain the triple lock on pensions.

Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).crime: The DUP focuses on fully staffing the PSNI and rooting out paramilitary activity. They demand consistent sentencing for terror offenses across the UK and stronger custodial terms for murder. Key pledges include a standalone offense for assaulting retail staff, repealing the Legacy Act, and establishing a UK-wide definition of a victim that excludes perpetrators. They also prioritize tackling online harm and grooming.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).healthcare: The DUP emphasizes fair funding for the NHS, based on assessed need in Northern Ireland. They aim to drive down waiting lists through large-scale partnerships and support for GPs, including a state-backed indemnity scheme. The party supports tackling smoking and vaping by raising the sale age to 21 and is committed to improving palliative care while opposing the legalization of assisted suicide and radical abortion laws.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).housing: The DUP aims to increase housing supply by launching an "Intermediate Rent" product for affordable rentals and raising value limits for Co-Ownership. They propose a national database of public land to help small construction firms identify projects. Other measures include addressing cladding issues, introducing defective premises legislation for homeowner protection, and reviewing how asylum accommodation contracts impact local housing needs in all UK regions.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).immigration: The DUP advocates for a firm, fair, and controlled UK-wide immigration policy governed by Westminster. They fight to ensure national asylum policies apply equally to Northern Ireland despite Protocol-related court rulings. Pledges include renewed efforts to smash smuggling gangs, more efficient asylum processing, and reviewing minimum salary thresholds for skilled workers to better reflect the Northern Ireland economy and its labour shortages.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).defence: The DUP advocates for spending 3% of GDP on defense by 2035 to meet rising global threats. They support safeguarding the nuclear deterrent and demand the greater integration of Northern Ireland into national defense structures, including an increased RAF and Royal Navy presence. They also aim to establish a defense and security cluster in Northern Ireland to boost MoD contracts and local STEM jobs.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).economy: The DUP focuses on "Making NI Work" within the UK internal market by removing trade barriers created by the Protocol. They demand a fair funding model for Northern Ireland based on assessed need. Economic pledges include lowering corporation tax, reducing VAT for the hospitality sector, and increasing the R&D tax credit. They also support SMEs by raising the VAT threshold to £100,000.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).education: The DUP focuses on "Making NI Work" by settling teacher pay disputes and investing in Special Educational Needs facilities. They support 22.5 hours of free pre-school education and £150m for the Strule Shared Education Campus. The party seeks to replace the Apprenticeship Levy with a ringfenced skills fund and proposes a twinning programme for primary schools across the United Kingdom.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).environment: The DUP supports a "fairer – not faster" path to net zero, emphasizing that decarbonization must be inclusive and economically responsible. They aim to double Northern Ireland’s low carbon economy and support a strategic national approach to clean energy production. Key environmental priorities include a recovery plan for Lough Neagh, tackling river pollution, and achieving a 70% recycling rate by 2030.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).brexit: The DUP seeks to fully restore Northern Ireland’s place within the United Kingdom by removing the internal Irish Sea border and the application of EU law. They strongly oppose the Northern Ireland Protocol and the Windsor Framework, arguing they have "wrecked the settled political balance". Their focus is on ensuring the primacy of the UK internal market and securing national immigration and trade policies.
Democratic Unionist Party (DUP).entire manifesto: The DUP's "Making NI Work" plan prioritizes promoting the Union and removing the internal Irish Sea border. They demand fair funding for Northern Ireland's NHS and public services based on assessed need. Economic goals include unleashing growth through industrial strategy and supporting family incomes by freezing duties. They are unashamedly pro-life, support victims' rights by repealing the Legacy Act, and want increased defence spending.

Sinn Féin.crime: Sinn Féin proposes the largest Garda recruitment drive in history, including a second training college to reach 16,000 officers. They focus on restorative justice, doubling investment in diversion programs, and establishing a Standards and Anti-Corruption Commission. Key priorities include tackling rural crime through increased patrolling, ensuring Gardaí are competent in the Irish language, and establishing dedicated Rape Crisis Centres for every 200,000 people.
Sinn Féin.healthcare: Sinn Féin’s "A Prescription for Change" plan proposes transitioning to universal healthcare, including free prescription medicines and medical cards for all up to median incomes. They pledge to deliver 5,000 hospital beds by 2031 and revolutionise youth mental health with integrated services. A major priority is using €2bn of "Apple Tax" money to build acute hospital beds and reduce waiting lists while hiring public GPs and dentists.
Sinn Féin.housing: Sinn Féin pledges the largest house-building programme in Irish history, delivering 300,000 homes by 2029, including 125,000 social and affordable units. They plan a three-year ban on rent increases and would provide a refundable tax credit worth one month's rent. Other policies include abolishing the Local Property Tax, phasing out Help to Buy, and holding a referendum to enshrine the Right to Housing.
Sinn Féin.immigration: Sinn Féin proposes establishing a new Immigration Management Agency to unify processing, enforcement, and accommodation under one department. They advocate for a system based on decency and the protection of human rights. Key priorities include ending the two-tier system, trebling staffing to speed up decisions, and ensuring asylum accommodation is state-owned and not placed in disadvantaged working-class communities. They also seek revised returns arrangements with Britain.
Sinn Féin.defence: Sinn Féin is committed to protecting Irish military neutrality through a constitutional amendment. They propose rebuilding the Irish Defence Forces to 11,500 personnel and increasing capital investment for radar and subsea capabilities. Their policy prioritizes UN-mandated peacekeeping missions, opposes further EU militarisation, and seeks to increase medical and financial support for veterans negatively impacted by their service.
Sinn Féin.economy: Sinn Féin proposes using windfall corporation tax and "Apple tax" money for a massive community and infrastructure investment fund. They aim to abolish the USC for average earners and increase the minimum wage to make work pay. Their strategy focuses on regional development and building a sustainable indigenous SME sector. They remain committed to maintaining the 12.5% corporation tax rate.
Sinn Féin.education: Sinn Féin views education as a public good and aims to make it truly free by phasing out private school subsidies and student fees. They prioritize Special Educational Needs with massive staff recruitment and propose €10-a-day childcare. Plans include expanding school transport, ending "voluntary contributions," and introducing an Activity Card for afterschool sport and arts participation.
Sinn Féin.environment: Sinn Féin seeks a transition from "eco-austerity to climate justice," targeting the carbon output of the wealthy. They propose a €2.5 billion Renewable Energy Investment Fund to establish state equity in green projects and an overhauled national retrofit program. To protect nature, they would establish a €300 million nature restoration fund, expand National Parks, and ban large-scale destructive factory fishing vessels.
Sinn Féin.brexit: Sinn Féin asserts that Ireland’s place is firmly within the European Union and that Brexit has made the case for Irish unity more urgent. They propose a "Plan for Unity," including referendums by the end of the decade, to ensure the whole of Ireland can benefit from EU membership. They aim to build support for reunification across the EU and maintain Ireland’s independent foreign policy.
Sinn Féin.entire manifesto: Sinn Féin's "Choice for Change" focuses on Irish unity, proposing referendums and planning for reunification. They pledge a massive public house-building programme (300,000 homes by 2029) and a transition to universal healthcare. Other priorities include €10-a-day childcare, abolishing the USC for average earners, and establishing a Renewable Energy Investment Fund. They also advocate for an independent foreign policy.
